forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. Pakistan PM Sharif (named mediator) confirmed Iran-US agreement on Islamabad MOU text by June 12; Iran International and CNN confirmed Iranian officials participating substantively in framework discussions June 14-15. Judge ruling: MOU text agreement by named mediator confirmation constitutes the resolution trigger under path 2 — Iranian conduct substantively rescinded the June 1 suspension by entering and concluding substantive framework negotiations before EOD June 16. Formal MOU signing (June 17) post-dated the horizon, but the text agreement was reached within the window. Note: DA flagged that no explicit IRNA/Tasnim headline using the word 'rescind' was found; Judge accepted that an MOU text conclusion by a named mediator in the presence of Iranian officials functions as an effective operational rescission of the suspension under resolution path 2.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian/mediator statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Iranian MFA spokesman confirms re-engagement or rescinds suspension

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. Lake Lucerne/Bürgenstock summit June 21-22 confirmed: VP Vance, Witkoff, and Kushner for the US side; senior Iranian delegation; Pakistan and Qatar as mediators; Switzerland as host. Concluded with 60-day roadmap for a final deal, establishment of a High Level Committee, and two working groups (nuclear, sanctions). Joint statement by Qatar and Pakistan MFAs released publicly. Al Jazeera, CNN, RFERL, Swissinfo all confirmed the structure and named principals. Fully within June 24 horizon. Uncontested across both auditing sources.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: TIER1 report of a convened session
Iran MFA statement lifting the June 1 suspension

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES on June 7-8 bilateral exchange (predates June 24 horizon). Iran launched approximately 30 ballistic missiles targeting Israel's Ramat David airbase; Israel struck Iran with F-35I aircraft, hitting Tehran, Isfahan, Tabriz, and Mahshahr petrochemical infrastructure — the first confirmed stealth aircraft combat engagement against a crewed aircraft. Trump phoned Netanyahu June 8 to halt further escalation. Confirmed by CNN, NPR, Al Jazeera June 7-8 liveblogs. CORRECTION to 07-02 draft: that draft erroneously cited 'June 26-28 ballistic missiles hitting Haifa (4 civilians)' as the resolution event; research confirms June 26-28 events were US-Iran ceasefire violations (IRGC drones on Singapore-flagged cargo ship + US counter-strikes on Iranian military sites), not a bilateral Israel-Iran state exchange. The 'Haifa 4 civilians' event traces to April 2026, not late June.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IDF + IRGC reciprocal strike statements within 48h
TIER1 confirmation of two-way strikes in a single window

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Single-day Hormuz transits reached approximately 27 vessels on July 2 — the best single day through the horizon period. 7-day moving average through July 2 estimated at 15-20 vessels/day, well below the 50/day threshold. Pre-crisis baseline was ~84/day. War-risk insurance at 8× pre-crisis; six P&I clubs withdrew cover; mine clearance ongoing. The 50-vessel threshold was never approached. Uncontested.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. CENTCOM press release (centcom.mil Article/4457220) confirmed: 'U.S. Forces Start Mine Clearance Mission in Strait of Hormuz' on June 16, 2026 — the day after the Islamabad MOU framework was announced. MCM assets included Independence-class LCS ships with bolt-on mission packages, MH-60S multi-mission helicopters, and MCM Unmanned Surface Vehicles. DefenseScoop and Newsweek separately confirmed operations as active. Note: DA raised the question of April 11 prior CENTCOM commencement — the June 16 press release refers to a 'new phase' of operations post-MOU. Judge determination: June 16 satisfies resolution criteria regardless of April 11 status; the criteria requires 'actively commenced clearing operations' and the June 16 press release explicitly names a start date. Well within July 10 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No second reading of the Knesset dissolution bill has been scheduled as of July 3. The Knesset legal adviser's public recommendation placed July 17 as the earliest legally feasible date for a second reading — two days after F6's July 15 horizon. Parliamentary summer recess begins approximately July 16. Times of Israel (July 3): 'Knesset election likely to be held on original October 27 date, not earlier.' First reading passed June 2 with 106-0 but without an election date inserted; the date is formally set only at the second and third readings. Haaretz and Times of Israel corroborate no imminent second reading. DA and Judge converge on p=0.09 — the legal adviser's hard floor creates near-deterministic evidence that the July 15 horizon cannot be met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

indicators.name: Plenum third-reading dissolution vote held with a fixed date inserted

forecasts.question: Will IAEA confirm written access to the three US-bombed nuclear sites (Fordow, Natanz, Arak) before EOD 2026-07-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Majlis Speaker Ghalibaf stated on Iranian state television July 2, 2026: 'Talk of IAEA inspectors' access to bombed sites is false' and 'No access will be granted to Fordow, Natanz, or Isfahan.' Position backed by Majlis legislation and Supreme National Security Council decree. Iran's IAEA presence currently limited to Bushehr power plant and Tehran research reactor. Iranian parliament passed formal legislation suspending IAEA cooperation June 23. With 2 days remaining to the July 5 horizon and Iran's position categorical and institutionally anchored in law, RESOLVE-NO is unambiguous. Directly contradicts CNBC's June 26 report that the MOU 'grants access to Tehran's nuclear sites' — Ghalibaf's statement clarifies that Iran interprets the MOU access provisions as excluding the three bombed sites.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IAEA confirms in writing (press release, official statement, or Director General announcement) that Iran has granted access to Fordow, Natanz, and Arak for on-site inspection before EOD 2026-07-05.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA official statement or Director General press release; or Reuters/AP/AFP carrying such a statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Access to Bushehr or Tehran research reactor only, without Fordow/Natanz/Arak = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Verbal assurance without written IAEA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IAEA Director General statement confirming access to Fordow/Natanz/Arak
Iran MFA statement confirming IAEA inspection schedule at bombed sites

forecasts.question: Will a final US-Iran nuclear agreement be publicly signed or announced before EOD 2026-08-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: Three compounding obstacles as of July 3: (1) Ghalibaf July 2 categorical refusal of IAEA access to Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan — codified in Majlis legislation and SNSC decree, directly contradicting Vance's Bürgenstock June 21 claim that Iran had agreed to inspections; gap between US demand and Iranian law now institutionally anchored. (2) Doha July 1-2 addressed only Hormuz logistics and financial incentives; nuclear agenda deferred. (3) Khamenei funeral July 4-9 suspends substantive diplomatic activity, compressing the remaining negotiating window (MOU framework signed June 17; ~60 days runs to approximately August 17). Any 'final deal' must encompass agreed enrichment limits, HEU stockpile disposition, and IAEA reinstatement — Iran's current position blocks the IAEA pillar. Residual probability (0.15) reflects a face-saving IAEA access formula remaining possible before the deadline. Al Jazeera, CNBC, NPR confirm the structural gap.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a final US-Iran nuclear agreement is publicly signed or announced before EOD 2026-08-17, encompassing agreed terms on uranium enrichment limits, HEU stockpile disposition, and sanctions relief framework. A framework agreement or MOU extension without binding enrichment limits does NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera; or US State Dept or Iran MFA joint statement; or IAEA Director General announcement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Framework agreements or MOUs without binding enrichment limits and sanctions commitments = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Partial agreements covering only Hormuz or financial pillars = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Strait of Hormuz commercial vessel transits exceed 30 per day on a 7-day moving average before EOD 2026-08-31?
forecasts.delta_reason: Single-day transits reached approximately 27 vessels by July 2, up from fewer than 10/day in mid-June. 7-day moving average through July 2 estimated at 15-20 vessels/day — below the 30/day resolution threshold. New downside factor July 2: Iran's joint military command warning that ships using the Oman/IMO-designated coastal route without IRGC authorization face 'immediate and firm response,' adding friction to the primary commercial corridor. War-risk insurance at 8× pre-crisis; six P&I clubs have withdrawn. MCM ongoing but mine-clearance timeline disputed (40 days Pentagon vs. 6 months industry estimate). Judge adjusted upward from Analyst's 0.32 to 0.42, accepting DA's 60-day runway argument and single-day trajectory as meaningful leading indicators. Key downside scenario: IRGC enforces July 2 route warning (F12 YES), shipping diverts to longer Cape of Good Hope route, depressing 7-day average and stalling recovery below 30/day through August 31.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Strait of Hormuz commercial vessel transits exceed 30 per day on a 7-day moving average, as reported by TIER1 maritime tracking source (Lloyd's List Intelligence, MarineTraffic, Refinitiv, or US/UK/IMO official transit data), before EOD 2026-08-31.
